tasks.short: Analyse capability gaps and recommend new or improved training programmes.

steps.what: Retrieve course participation, assessment results and completion records from the {LMS}.
Read survey responses, validated training needs and role requirements in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Survey responses, validated training needs and role requirements.
loop.output: Evidence-linked themes, reported gaps and conflicting accounts.
loop.check: Require source references; check missing responses and review conflicts without inferring individual capability.
loop.stop: One pass and one repair per document batch; unsupported claims return to manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text descriptions express similar needs differently and often contain qualifications.

steps.what: Compare learning results and reported gaps by cohort in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Discuss whether gaps arise from skills, workload, tools or unclear expectations.
Develop programme options, objectives and evaluation measures in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Gap diagnosis, existing courses, evaluation findings and budget constraints.
loop.output: Comparable programme options with objectives, delivery choices and evaluation measures.
loop.check: Check costs against supplied rates, trace objectives to gaps and review practical suitability.
loop.stop: At most three options and one revision; missing costs remain explicitly unknown.
loop.why_not_simpler: Connecting contextual needs to learning activities requires bounded drafting beyond a fixed template.

steps.what: Select priorities and approve a programme brief within delegated authority.

tasks.design: Configure an export from the {LMS}, combine it with approved needs evidence on the {DATA_PLATFORM}, and publish cohort comparisons in the {BI}. Bounded loops prepare evidence summaries and programme options in the {DOCS}; the manager diagnoses causes and approves the programme brief.
tasks.previous_blocker: Learning records and qualitative needs were separate. Analysis also depended on local knowledge that reporting alone could not supply.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports, reusable data mappings and faster code development make the reporting practical. Bounded text extraction can reduce reading without claiming to diagnose capability automatically.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing a training need from an operational problem remains difficult. Small cohorts, inconsistent assessments and confidential comments limit useful comparisons.
tasks.human_edge: The manager challenges requests for training when better tools, clearer expectations or workload changes would help more.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling evidence to testing diagnoses and comparing interventions. Monthly prioritisation becomes feasible; formal budget and programme approval rights change only through explicit delegation.

reach.task: Identify role-specific onboarding gaps before new starters enter training.
reach.learn: Learn onboarding triggers, role requirements and the distinction between mandatory and optional learning.

evidence.claim: Structured learning exports and fixed cohort calculations can support needs analysis; proposed savings are estimates.
A study covering HR and other occupations found modest average chatbot time savings; it does not validate these task estimates.
GDPR Article 22 constrains solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects on employees.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining-time percentages are planning estimates informed by the supplied priors.
The initial scope uses cohort evidence rather than automated individual capability ratings.
The {LMS} supports scheduled exports; unavailable exports would require deterministic integration.
Build ranges cover one pilot business unit, existing hosting and a limited course catalogue.
GDPR applies to employee data. National rules may require consultation about new employee-data uses.
unknowns: Which learning records, assessments and role requirements are available and reliable?
What cohort sizes and access restrictions apply?
Who can approve programme changes and budget commitments?
Which country and employee-representation arrangements apply?
research_questions: Which cohort suppression and aggregation practices fit the intended analysis?
Which national consultation requirements cover the proposed employee-data use?
new_work: Review evidence summaries and unresolved conflicts.
Maintain cohort mappings, calculation definitions and source permissions.
Check whether recommended interventions address the diagnosed cause.
Monitor access logs and retention of qualitative comments.

tasks.short: Evaluate instructors and programme effectiveness, then agree improvements.

steps.what: Retrieve attendance, assessment results and feedback responses from the {LMS}.
Observe instruction, practice activities and learner participation.
Read learner comments and observation notes in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Learner comments and instruction observation notes.
loop.output: Source-linked themes, contrary examples and questions requiring follow-up.
loop.check: Review cited excerpts, preserve minority views and exclude inferred instructor ratings.
loop.stop: One pass and one repair per course batch; ambiguous or sensitive comments receive manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Comments contain mixed meanings and context that fixed keyword rules miss.

steps.what: Calculate completion, assessment change and response rates in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Discuss evidence with the instructor and determine a fair performance assessment.
Draft recommendations for content, delivery and instructor support in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Human instructor assessment, evidence summary and calculated programme outcomes.
loop.output: Recommendations linked to evidence, with uncertainty and proposed follow-up measures.
loop.check: Reject unsupported causal claims, invented costs and changes to the human instructor assessment.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; disputed interpretations return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Recommendations must connect varied evidence to contextual teaching changes.

steps.what: Agree improvement actions, owners and review dates with the instructor.

tasks.design: Feed configured exports from the {LMS} into deterministic outcome calculations on the {DATA_PLATFORM} and a restricted {BI} dashboard. Bounded loops summarise comments and draft recommendations in the {DOCS}; observation, instructor assessment and agreement on improvements remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Feedback, observations and learning outcomes were hard to compare. Collecting them did not resolve whether teaching caused the observed results.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable calculations and evidence-linked text summaries reduce preparation. Faster implementation makes a small evaluation dashboard affordable without requiring automated personnel scoring.
tasks.still_hard: Response bias, small samples and differences between learner groups complicate evaluation. Fair instructor assessment needs context and an opportunity to challenge evidence.
tasks.human_edge: The manager distinguishes poor instruction from unsuitable content, learner circumstances or weak measurement and gives constructive feedback.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time observing teaching and checking whether improvements worked. Faster evidence supports monthly course decisions; employment and supplier-contract decisions retain their existing approval routes.

reach.task: Assess whether learning access and outcomes differ unfairly between employee groups.
reach.learn: Learn safe cohort aggregation, reasonable adjustments and the limits of outcome comparisons.

evidence.claim: Fixed outcome calculations and bounded comment summaries can reduce evaluation preparation; savings and build ranges are estimates.
GDPR Article 22 is relevant where instructor assessments produce significant employment effects.
AI intended to monitor or evaluate worker performance may fall within the AI Act employment category.
AI Act Article 26 includes worker information obligations for workplace deployment of high-risk AI.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining-time percentages are planning estimates informed by the supplied priors.
The initial design calculates programme measures and summarises evidence without generating individual performance scores.
The {LMS} holds evaluation responses and supports exports.
Build ranges cover a small programme pilot with agreed measures and existing hosting.
GDPR applies; AI Act classification depends on intended use. National consultation rules require separate assessment.
unknowns: Are instructors employees, external providers or both?
What employment consequences can an instructor assessment have?
Which baseline measures and follow-up outcomes exist?
Are observations and learner comments collected under an established policy?
Which country, representatives and approval arrangements apply?
research_questions: Which evaluation design can distinguish learning effects from differences between cohorts?
Does the intended use constitute worker-performance evaluation under the EU AI Act?
Which national rules govern consultation and access to instructor assessments?
new_work: Review comment summaries and contested evidence.
Maintain calculation definitions and observation rubrics.
Investigate missing responses and misleading cohort comparisons.
Track improvement actions and measure their later effects.
Maintain restricted access and respond to correction requests.

tasks.short: Design, organise and deliver training that develops staff capability.

steps.what: Choose learning objectives, delivery methods and evaluation measures in the {DOCS}.
Develop explanations, demonstrations, exercises and facilitator guidance in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved source material, delivery plan and learning templates.
loop.output: A learning package with source-linked explanations, exercises and facilitator guidance.
loop.check: Check every objective is covered; review factual support, accessibility and exercise answers.
loop.stop: One draft and two revisions per module; unsupported technical content goes to the expert.
loop.why_not_simpler: Useful explanations and realistic exercises require contextual writing beyond template population.

steps.what: Check technical accuracy and safe practice in the learning package.
Approve the learning package for delivery.
Publish approved sessions and enrol eligible learners in the {LMS}.
Facilitate demonstrations, practice, discussion and feedback.
Record attendance and verified learning results in the {LMS}.
Discuss workplace application and barriers with learners and their managers.

tasks.design: Use approved sources and templates in the {DOCS} for bounded drafting of learning packages, with technical and delivery approval before publication. Configure the {LMS} to publish approved sessions, manage enrolment and record verified results; instructors deliver practice and managers discuss workplace application.
tasks.previous_blocker: Materials required repeated writing and revision. Existing course administration could automate logistics but could not judge technical accuracy or adapt instruction to learners.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can accelerate material development, while existing enrolment and completion functions can be configured. Faster code development helps connect approved packages to course administration.
tasks.still_hard: Specialist content, accessible exercises and effective practice require careful design. Attendance does not establish competence, and workplace application depends on supervisors and available practice.
tasks.human_edge: An instructor notices confusion, adjusts the explanation and creates a setting where learners can practise and ask difficult questions.
tasks.altitude: Less time goes to first drafts and course administration, leaving more time for practice and follow-up. A transfer clinic adds a service; authority over programme methods remains within the existing delegation.

reach.task: Design and run a supervisor-supported follow-up session after training.
reach.learn: Learn practice design, facilitator coaching and how to observe workplace application without creating employee scores.

evidence.claim: Course publication, enrolment and learning-record administration are commonly configurable functions of an {LMS}.
Source-grounded drafting can prepare learning materials, but experts still need to verify technical content.
The digest provides no documented training-delivery case validating the proposed time savings or build ranges.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining-time percentages are planning estimates informed by the supplied priors.
The manager coordinates delivery and may also teach; step shares include supporting roles.
The pilot covers one programme with available source material and established expert reviewers.
The {LMS} supports session administration, rule-based enrolment and structured result capture.
Only approved eligibility rules drive enrolment; no model assigns employees to opportunities.
GDPR applies to learner records. National consultation requirements depend on changes to learning and employee-data practices.
unknowns: Which course formats and enrolment functions are already supported?
Who owns source material and can approve its reuse?
Which subjects require accredited instructors or formal competency assessment?
What accessibility and language needs must the programme meet?
Can supervisors provide workplace practice and attend follow-up sessions?
Which country and consultation arrangements apply?
research_questions: Which accessibility and assessment standards apply to the proposed learning materials?
What follow-up design best supports workplace application for the chosen programme?
new_work: Review draft content, exercises and source references.
Maintain approved sources and regenerate affected modules when they change.
Handle enrolment exceptions and incorrect session results.
Check that recorded completion matches the required evidence.
Coordinate and evaluate the learning transfer clinic.

tasks.short: Consult managers and survey employees to identify training needs from planned operational changes.

steps.what: Read operational change plans and role requirements in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Operational change plans and role requirements.
loop.output: Source-linked changes, affected roles, dates and questions for management.
loop.check: Verify dates and role references; preserve uncertainty about unapproved plans.
loop.stop: One pass and one repair per plan; missing or conflicting details go to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative plans describe process changes inconsistently and rarely specify learning implications directly.

steps.what: Prepare and approve survey questions about expected tasks, confidence and support needs.

loop.input: Consultation brief and an approved survey template.
loop.output: Short, neutral survey questions tied to the planned changes.
loop.check: The manager checks relevance, leading wording and unnecessary personal-data collection before approval.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; sensitive or disputed questions are written manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed template provides the structure, but questions need contextual wording for each change.

steps.what: Launch the survey, monitor responses and send reminders through the {WORKFLOW}.
Confer with operational managers about changing work, constraints and capability expectations.
Combine survey findings and management needs notes in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Survey responses, management needs notes and the consultation brief.
loop.output: A training needs draft distinguishing agreement, conflicting views and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Trace each proposed need to evidence; calculate response counts deterministically and flag underrepresented groups.
loop.stop: One synthesis and one repair; unresolved disagreements remain questions for validation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reconciling narrative accounts requires interpretation; fixed counts cannot resolve differing meanings.

steps.what: Validate expected work changes, affected roles and unresolved needs with the training manager.

tasks.design: Configure approved surveys and reminders in the {WORKFLOW}, and keep change plans and consultation records in the {DOCS}. Bounded loops prepare briefs, survey wording and evidence-linked needs drafts; managers discuss the changes and validate the resulting needs before programme analysis.
tasks.previous_blocker: Operational plans were incomplete and managers expressed needs differently. Survey administration was easier to standardise than the conversations needed to clarify changing work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms and reminders handle collection. Bounded reading and drafting make consultation preparation and synthesis cheaper while retaining human discussion.
tasks.still_hard: Managers may disagree about future work or describe preferences as capability gaps. Survey participation, confidentiality and uncertainty in change plans require attention.
tasks.human_edge: The manager asks follow-up questions, surfaces disagreement and builds enough trust for employees and managers to describe actual difficulties.

ambition.what: Pre-launch learning-readiness review for operational changes

tasks.altitude: More of the week goes to clarifying future work and testing assumptions with managers. Earlier readiness reviews can influence change plans, but they confer no automatic veto or budget authority.

reach.task: Include learning readiness in workforce planning for an operational change.
reach.learn: Learn change milestones, role-impact assessment and how to distinguish learning support from staffing changes.

reach.task: Plan employee consultation when changes affect work practices or employee-data collection.
reach.learn: Learn representative involvement, confidentiality expectations and applicable national consultation procedures.

evidence.claim: Configured surveys and reminders can automate collection while consultation and validation remain human.
Bounded text extraction and synthesis can prepare consultation evidence; the proposed savings are estimates.
The cited Dutch works-council law includes consent provisions for employee-data and monitoring arrangements; national rules elsewhere vary.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining-time percentages are planning estimates informed by the supplied priors.
The company already has a form capability in the {WORKFLOW}; otherwise a small deterministic form is required.
The pilot concerns one planned operational change and uses manually selected source documents.
No meetings are recorded automatically; reviewed notes provide the input.
Surveys identify group needs rather than rank individual employees.
GDPR applies. National rules determine whether employee or works-council consultation is required.
unknowns: Which operational changes and affected roles are sufficiently defined?
Can employees respond confidentially, and who may read raw responses?
Which employee groups need alternative ways to participate?
Which form capabilities and source-document access already exist?
Which country and employee-representation arrangements apply?
Who validates operational assumptions and owns unresolved questions?
research_questions: Which survey design reduces leading questions and nonresponse bias for this audience?
Which national consultation requirements apply to the planned work and data changes?
new_work: Approve contextual survey wording and maintain templates.
Review extracted changes and conflicting dates.
Check participation gaps and arrange alternative consultation.
Review synthesis for omitted concerns and unsupported conclusions.
Maintain access, retention and confidentiality settings.

role.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling evidence, drafting routine material and administering courses, and more time diagnosing needs, observing instruction and supporting workplace application. More frequent programme decisions become feasible; formal spending, employment and change-approval rights require explicit delegation.
reach: Help human resources specialists connect onboarding needs to role-specific learning.
Work with equal opportunity officers to investigate aggregate differences in learning access and outcomes.
Help human resources managers assess learning readiness before operational changes launch.
Work with labor relations specialists on consultation for changed work and employee-data practices.
skills_to_grow: Diagnosing capability gaps versus operational constraints
Defining defensible learning and transfer measures
Reviewing source-grounded drafts and qualitative summaries
Configuring learning workflows and maintaining data definitions
Designing accessible practice and coaching supervisors
Understanding GDPR, EU AI Act intended-use classification and applicable national rules
role.ambitious_version: Run a learning-readiness and transfer service that connects planned work changes to practical learning, supervisor-supported practice and evidence-led programme improvements.
